clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old female presented with a 4-day history of a painless lump in the posterior right thigh. Comprehensive imaging workup on admission revealed a 6.1 × 9.6 × 9.8 cm calcified mass in the posteromedial soft tissues of the right thigh with imaging characteristics highly suspicious for ESOS: plain radiographs showed a calcified mass with ill-defined central calcification; targeted ultrasound demonstrated a hypoechoic mass with dense calcification and posterior acoustic shadowing; MRI showed a heterogeneously enhancing mass with infiltrative margins; CT confirmed central calcification with ill-defined mineralization and peripheral margins; and bone scintigraphy demonstrated abnormally increased uptake in the mass. Tissue sampling under Orthopedic guidance was performed and confirmed the diagnosis of extraskeletal osteosarcoma. Staging CT imaging showed no evidence of metastatic disease in the chest, abdomen, and pelvis.
